Change over an interval

Placeholder paragraph for the test fixture. The average rate of change of a function on an interval is the change in its output divided by the change in its input, $\frac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a}$. On a graph it is the slope of the secant line through the two points. A positive rate means the output rises as the input rises; a negative rate means it falls. Comparing average rates over small intervals near two points tells which point the function changes faster at, and how those rates change from one interval to the next tells whether the graph bends up or down.
